1	# Handoff: G-code and print history
2	
3	Written 2026-10-27, rewritten the same evening after Kenneth and I redesigned it. Temporary working doc: keep it untracked, never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
4	
5	## In short
6	
7	JusPrin keeps **one record per G-code** that left a project: where it went (exported files, sends to printers) and what the printer reported about each print of it (printing, finished). Slicing by itself writes nothing. **No failure state anywhere** (decided 2026-10-27): there is no reliable way to know a print failed, so nothing records, badges or discusses a failure.
8	
9	That record is shown on **one full-view screen, "Print history"**, reached from Home and from the project. The chat only gets a one-line marker when a G-code leaves the project. The old design, where the chat held G-code entries and a dark failed-print band, is retired: its boards are deleted or redrawn. A print that went wrong is something the person tells the agent in chat; the history gives the G-code and its settings for that conversation.
10	
11	The app is far behind: it persists `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` but never writes them outside tests, has no export record, and the model never sees print history. The next job is to implement the drawn design.
12	
13	## Where the design lives
14	
15	- **Current canvas, the source of truth:** https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ ("JusPrin v2"), version 1793148719-e71c or later (checked against the published file list on 2026-10-27: history-01…05 present, history-06 and agent-ui-01 gone, comp-plates-pane, main-05/07/09 and plates-26e3 updated). New page **"Print history"** (id `print-history`):
16	  - `history-01-all-prints`: the screen with no filter.
17	  - `history-02-project-garage-bracket`: filtered to one project.
18	  - `history-03-printer-bambu-x1c`: filtered to one printer.
19	  - `history-04-entry-states`: every row state of an entry, and the no-failure-state rule. This replaces the deleted `agent-ui-01` chat-timeline state matrix.
20	  - `history-05-ways-in`: the Home header link, project cards, printer cards and the project pane row that open the screen.
21	  - (`history-06-discuss-in-current-chat` was drawn and deleted the same day when failure states were dropped.)
22	  - Main Page: `main-05`, `main-07`, `main-09` now show one-line G-code markers in the chat instead of entries and a band.
23	  - Plates & Project Pane: `plates-26e3` ("Project · print history row") and `plates-26e4` ("Project · never printed"; the file is still named `count-only-print-history`). Both import `comp-plates-pane`, whose Project tab was redrawn.
24	- **Frozen, history only:** the previous canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, the old Claude Design project "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts", and Figma (retired 2026-10-20). They show the chat-entry design and how it was reached, never the current design.
25	- Memory note for agents: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/print-history-screen-design.md`.
26	
27	## The design (decided 2026-10-27)
28	
29	### The record
30	
31	Every print has three keys: the project it came from, the G-code it ran, and the printer it ran on. That is one table. The project view and the printer view are filters over it, so they can never disagree.
32	
33	The **G-code record** (decided 2026-10-27 in a forked session, relayed here by that session; Kenneth's words were "go with your recommendations"):
34	
35	- **Identity:** a hash of the G-code file bytes, computed at export or send time, before the file leaves. The existing `manufacturing_input_hash` stays beside it as the link to the checkpoint. Displayed as eight hex digits in two groups ("a71f 8c04").
36	- **Shape:** one record per G-code holding its lists of destinations (exports, sends) and prints. Export and send create the record or append to it. The separate `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` events are replaced, not kept beside it.
37	- **Bytes:** JusPrin keeps a copy of every sent or exported G-code in the project's aux directory next to the checkpoints, capped at the last N G-codes per project (N chosen in code). Older entries show a "file no longer kept, re-slice" state instead of Print again.
38	
39	An **entry** is one G-code:
40	
41	- Header: name (the exported file name, else the plate name), short hash in monospace as a secondary id, the stats line ("2h 34m · 69 g · 181 layers"), the time. The project name shows only when no project filter is on.
42	- "Made with Bambu X1C · Gray PETG · 0.20 Strong · Open in chat". Open in chat jumps to the marker in the chat where this G-code went out.
43	- One row per **destination**:
44	  - Export: `matches, checked just now` (green check); `changed outside JusPrin` (greyed, warning glyph, Export again); `not found` (greyed, Export again). Greyed means opacity, never strike-through. Export again writes a new file beside a changed one, it does not overwrite.
45	  - Send: `sending…`; `sent, delivery not confirmed`; `on the printer's SD · started` or `· not started`. A send never gets a check mark: only a hashed file is verified. Use the printer's own name, not its model.
46	- One row per **print**, only what the printer reports: Printing (the only live fact drawn; progress stays on the printer card) and Finished. **No Failed, Didn't go well or Cancelled row.** Kenneth, 2026-10-27: "I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed." Cancelled goes with them because a Bambu reports a person's stop as a failed state and the two cannot be told apart. A print that stopped early simply never gets a Finished row.
47	- Actions: **Print again** and **Export…**. Reprint lives only here. Kenneth: the common question is "which version am I printing", so a reprint must be attached to a specific G-code, never to a project or a printer.
48	
49	### The screen
50	
51	- Full view in place of the plater, like Home. Top bar: back arrow, "Print history", preferences gear. No printer chip, no plate button.
52	- Home and Project are the roots; Print history is always a leaf. Back returns to where it was opened from. Nothing opens on top of it: Open in chat and the printer link go to a root.
53	- Filters are removable chips ("Project: Garage bracket ×", "Printer: Bambu X1C ×"). Where you came from sets the first chip; remove it and the list widens to everything. Entries are grouped by day, newest first. A search box filters by text.
54	
55	### Ways in
56	
57	- Home header: a "Print history" link, unfiltered.
58	- Each Home project card: a history line ("2 prints · 1 printing now", "1 print · finished Sun") that opens the screen filtered to the project. No failure badge.
59	- Each Home printer card: a history line ("12 prints · 1 printing now") filtered to the printer.
60	- Project pane, Project tab: the Print history view is now one row (count, latest outcome) with a chevron into the screen. A project that never printed says "Nothing printed or exported yet".
61	
62	### The chat
63	
64	- When a G-code leaves the project, one marker line between turns: "▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history". Nothing else.
65	- Nothing about a print going wrong is recorded or drawn anywhere. The person tells the agent in chat ("it shifted off the plate"); the agent reads the recent G-codes and their settings from the history in its state and reasons from there. There is no Discuss link, no attachment and no recording tool.
66	
67	### What is deliberately not drawn
68	
69	- No Stale badge, no live progress card, no completed-print card in the chat, no entry with zero destinations, no failure state of any kind. Slicing writes nothing.
70	
71	## Decision history
72	
73	| When | What happened |
74	|---|---|
75	| Aug 7 – Sep 1 | Old Design project: setup card, "Prints" chip, "the chat is the timeline". Phase 6 (51a97b1bdf, 2026-09-01) adds BuildRecord, ExportedCopyRecord, PhysicalPrintRecord with chat cards. |
76	| Sep 10 | Kenneth: slicing writes nothing; entries only for G-code that left the project; no Stale. |
77	| Sep 11 | "Revert here" removed (dcb06059f3). |
78	| Oct 2–3 | Print history moves to the Project tab in the left pane (`Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp`). |
79	| Oct 26 | dbec3e3a38 removes BuildRecord and ExportedCopyRecord, adds `SentRecord`. 71c1791e39 (docs only) specifies that sending goes through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog and that an agent tool `print_dialog_open` may open it; the tool was never implemented. |
80	| Oct 27 morning | Canvas named the source of truth; chat-entry boards redrawn (G-code entry with rows, failed-print band). |
81	| Oct 27 evening | Redesign with Kenneth. Reasons, in his words: reprint belongs to the specific G-code, not the project; a failure in an old chat is strange when the person is in a new one; the history page is the natural home for the story and for file verification; printer and project histories are one table with two filters; a full view, since a column makes the navigation strange. Boards drawn and old ones retired the same day. |
82	| Oct 27 later | In a forked session Kenneth settled the record: file-bytes hash as the id, one record with destination and print lists replacing the separate events, G-code copies kept in the aux dir with a cap. Relayed to this doc by that session. |
83	| Oct 27 later still | In another forked session Kenneth removed every failure state ("I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed"): no Failed / Didn't go well rows, no badge, no Discuss, history-06 deleted. Relayed by that session; this session dropped Cancelled with them. |
84	
85	## What the code does today (branch `jusprin-newui`, checked 2026-10-27 at 74951a60fd)
86	
87	Paths below are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Line numbers are from this checkout and will drift.
88	
89	### The ledger that exists but is never written
90	
91	- `Agent/ManufacturingHistory.hpp`: `SentRecord` (sent_at, delivery_confirmed_at, conversation_id, plate, printer, material, `manufacturing_input_hash`, statistics) and `PhysicalPrintRecord` (outcome completed | failed | cancelled, failure, sent_id, conversation_id, after_message_id, `output_hash`, `gcode_hash`, stopped_percent, statistics). `ManufacturingHistory.cpp:14` has `sha256_hex()` and `:25` `manufacturing_input_hash()`, which hash the plate's presets and transforms, not an output file. `output_hash` and `gcode_hash` are serialized (`ProjectStateDocument.cpp:269`, `:1039`) but nothing computes them.
92	- `Agent/ProjectStateDocument.hpp:264-275`: `add_sent`, `confirm_delivery`, `add_physical_print`, `sent()`, `physical_prints()`. A print must point at an existing Sent event. `Agent/ProjectPersistence.hpp:87-92`: `subscribe_ledger` / `notify_ledger_changed`, used by the left pane (`Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp:124`).
93	- **No production code calls any of the writers.** Only `tests/agent/test_project_state.cpp` and `tests/shell/figma_timeline_fixture.cpp:113` do.
94	
95	### Readers of the ledger, all to be redrawn
96	
97	- `Home/ProjectStatus.cpp:5` `ledger_status`: Draft / Sent / Completed from the latest Sent event and latest completed print. Failed and cancelled are ignored. "Printing" comes from the live printer, not the ledger (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:242-267` matches a printer's `subtask_name` to the project name).
98	- `Shell/ProjectPaneModel.cpp` `build_print_history` and `Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp`: the old Print history list in the Project tab.
99	- `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:782` `send_state` sends `physicalPrints` (`:872`, built by `physical_print_json` at `:192`); Sent events are not sent to the page. `AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx:112` renders `ManufacturingHistoryCard` from them (`:206`); its "Discuss this failure" is a plain `sendMessage` in `AgentUI/src/App.tsx:498`. Types: `PhysicalPrintInfo` (`AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts:721`) and `StatePayload.physicalPrints` (`:1002`). All of this goes away; the chat keeps only the marker line.
100	
101	### Export: where a file leaves
102	
103	- OrcaSlicer's export: `src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:15051` `Plater::export_gcode` fixes the output path, `Plater::priv::export_gcode` (`:8226`, `:8259`) schedules `BackgroundSlicingProcess::export_gcode` (`src/slic3r/GUI/BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:857`), which copies the temp G-code to the final path and queues `EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED` with that path (`:899`). **Trap:** it runs `gcode_add_line_number` after posting the event, so the bytes can still change after the event; hash after the process reports completion (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `Plater.cpp:9911`, which already shows the "export finished" notification from `last_output_path` at `:10043`). `Plater::priv::on_export_finished` (`:9825`) is bound at `:5298` and its body is `#if 0`.
104	- Sliced 3MF export: `Plater::export_gcode_3mf` (`:15157`) writes synchronously through `export_3mf` (`:15221`).
105	- JusPrin's `export_file` tool: defined in `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1256` (handler `ToolHandler::ExportFile`, in-app and MCP), dispatched in `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1726`, written by `Workspace/OrcaOutputs.cpp:346` `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::export_file` (a `copy_file` of the plate's slice result for G-code; `Plater::export_3mf` for 3MF). Its `ExportResult` (`Workspace/Workspace.hpp:1072`) has paths and sizes, no hash. The tool's result JSON carries `files`, `bytes`, `sliceWarnings`, no hash.
106	
107	### Send: where a file goes to a printer
108	
109	- The Print action in the status row (`Shell/StatusRow.cpp:584`) fires `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_PRINT_PLATE`, handled by `Plater::priv::on_action_print_plate` (`Plater.cpp:10251`).
110	- Bambu, Select Machine dialog (Send always starts the print): `src/slic3r/GUI/SelectMachine.cpp:2381` `on_send_print` builds a `PrintJob` (`:2471`), runs it (`:2588`); on success `PrintJob::process` queues `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/PrintJob.cpp:668`), handled by `Plater::print_job_finished` (`Plater.cpp:16575`).
111	- Bambu, Send to Printer dialog (upload to SD only, never prints): `src/slic3r/GUI/SendToPrinter.cpp:809` `on_ok` creates a `SendJob` (`:951`); `SendJob` queues `EVT_SEND_FINISHED` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/SendJob.cpp:364`), handled by `Plater::send_job_finished` (`Plater.cpp:16602`).
112	- Print hosts (Moonraker, OctoPrint): `Plater::send_gcode_legacy` (`Plater.cpp:16304`) reads the dialog's `post_action` (`:16473`; `StartPrint` = print after upload), stored in `PrintHostJob.upload_data.post_action` (`src/slic3r/Utils/PrintHost.hpp:39`). The upload completes in `PrintHostJobQueue::priv::perform_job` (`src/slic3r/Utils/PrintHost.cpp:357`, `emit_progress(100)` at `:368`), which reaches `PrintHostQueueDialog::on_progress` (`src/slic3r/GUI/PrintHostDialogs.cpp:1382`). There is no other success callback.
113	- **The fork binds none of `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, `EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED` or the print-host events.**
114	- **Correction to earlier notes:** commit 71c1791e39 ("Send a print through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog") changed three docs only. The `print_dialog_open` tool exists as a specification in `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:571` (seams named there: `Plater::priv::on_action_print_plate`, `Plater::send_gcode_legacy`) and nowhere in code.
115	
116	### Printer status: where outcomes would come from
117	
118	- Bambu fields in `src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceManager.hpp`: `print_status` (`:478`; FINISH, RUNNING, PAUSE, FAILED…), `mc_print_stage` (`:393`), `mc_print_percent` (`:397`), `print_error` (`:404`), `job_id_` / `task_id_` (`:643`), `subtask_name` (`:673`). Parsed in `MachineObject::parse_json` (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceManager.cpp:2569`; percent `:3069`, error `:3096`, state via `set_print_state` `:3185`, subtask name `:3196`). Messages arrive through `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:2157` (cloud) and `:2203` (LAN).
119	- The fork only polls these: `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:48` `machine_is_printing`, polled by `Home/HomeWebView.cpp:119` `on_live_tick` while Home is visible; also `PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp:78`, `Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:278`, `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:781`. **No fork class observes status changes.** A writer of printing / finished (FAILED and a person's stop are ignored on purpose) must hook `DeviceManager` / `GUI_App` message handling or poll `get_my_machine_list()` on its own timer, and must run whether or not Home or the project is visible.
120	- Matching a printer's job to a G-code record: today Home matches `subtask_name` to the project name. The new record should store what the send gave the printer (the uploaded file name, Bambu's job or task id when the job reports one) so a status change maps to one record, not to a project.
121	- Moonraker / Klipper: `Printers/HostLaneReader.cpp:53` `LaneReader` (a subclass of Orca's `Moonraker`) polls filament lanes only; `HostStatus` (`Printers/HostLanes.hpp:70`) has no print progress, and Orca's `src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp` never queries `print_stats`. Print-host outcomes need a new reader; the fake Moonraker simulator lives on branch `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under `tests/printer_sim/`.

# Handoff: G-code and print history

Written 2026-10-27, rewritten the same evening after Kenneth and I redesigned it. Temporary working doc: keep it untracked, never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.

## In short

JusPrin keeps **one record per G-code** that left a project: where it went (exported files, sends to printers) and what the printer reported about each print of it (printing, finished). Slicing by itself writes nothing. **No failure state anywhere** (decided 2026-10-27): there is no reliable way to know a print failed, so nothing records, badges or discusses a failure.

That record is shown on **one full-view screen, "Print history"**, reached from Home and from the project. The chat only gets a one-line marker when a G-code leaves the project. The old design, where the chat held G-code entries and a dark failed-print band, is retired: its boards are deleted or redrawn. A print that went wrong is something the person tells the agent in chat; the history gives the G-code and its settings for that conversation.

The app is far behind: it persists `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` but never writes them outside tests, has no export record, and the model never sees print history. The next job is to implement the drawn design.

## Where the design lives

- **Current canvas, the source of truth:** https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ ("JusPrin v2"), version 1793148719-e71c or later (checked against the published file list on 2026-10-27: history-01…05 present, history-06 and agent-ui-01 gone, comp-plates-pane, main-05/07/09 and plates-26e3 updated). New page **"Print history"** (id `print-history`):
  - `history-01-all-prints`: the screen with no filter.
  - `history-02-project-garage-bracket`: filtered to one project.
  - `history-03-printer-bambu-x1c`: filtered to one printer.
  - `history-04-entry-states`: every row state of an entry, and the no-failure-state rule. This replaces the deleted `agent-ui-01` chat-timeline state matrix.
  - `history-05-ways-in`: the Home header link, project cards, printer cards and the project pane row that open the screen.
  - (`history-06-discuss-in-current-chat` was drawn and deleted the same day when failure states were dropped.)
  - Main Page: `main-05`, `main-07`, `main-09` now show one-line G-code markers in the chat instead of entries and a band.
  - Plates & Project Pane: `plates-26e3` ("Project · print history row") and `plates-26e4` ("Project · never printed"; the file is still named `count-only-print-history`). Both import `comp-plates-pane`, whose Project tab was redrawn.
- **Frozen, history only:** the previous canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, the old Claude Design project "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts", and Figma (retired 2026-10-20). They show the chat-entry design and how it was reached, never the current design.
- Memory note for agents: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/print-history-screen-design.md`.

## The design (decided 2026-10-27)

### The record

Every print has three keys: the project it came from, the G-code it ran, and the printer it ran on. That is one table. The project view and the printer view are filters over it, so they can never disagree.

The **G-code record** (decided 2026-10-27 in a forked session, relayed here by that session; Kenneth's words were "go with your recommendations"):

- **Identity:** a hash of the G-code file bytes, computed at export or send time, before the file leaves. The existing `manufacturing_input_hash` stays beside it as the link to the checkpoint. Displayed as eight hex digits in two groups ("a71f 8c04").
- **Shape:** one record per G-code holding its lists of destinations (exports, sends) and prints. Export and send create the record or append to it. The separate `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` events are replaced, not kept beside it.
- **Bytes:** JusPrin keeps a copy of every sent or exported G-code in the project's aux directory next to the checkpoints, capped at the last N G-codes per project (N chosen in code). Older entries show a "file no longer kept, re-slice" state instead of Print again.

An **entry** is one G-code:

- Header: name (the exported file name, else the plate name), short hash in monospace as a secondary id, the stats line ("2h 34m · 69 g · 181 layers"), the time. The project name shows only when no project filter is on.
- "Made with Bambu X1C · Gray PETG · 0.20 Strong · Open in chat". Open in chat jumps to the marker in the chat where this G-code went out.
- One row per **destination**:
  - Export: `matches, checked just now` (green check); `changed outside JusPrin` (greyed, warning glyph, Export again); `not found` (greyed, Export again). Greyed means opacity, never strike-through. Export again writes a new file beside a changed one, it does not overwrite.
  - Send: `sending…`; `sent, delivery not confirmed`; `on the printer's SD · started` or `· not started`. A send never gets a check mark: only a hashed file is verified. Use the printer's own name, not its model.
- One row per **print**, only what the printer reports: Printing (the only live fact drawn; progress stays on the printer card) and Finished. **No Failed, Didn't go well or Cancelled row.** Kenneth, 2026-10-27: "I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed." Cancelled goes with them because a Bambu reports a person's stop as a failed state and the two cannot be told apart. A print that stopped early simply never gets a Finished row.
- Actions: **Print again** and **Export…**. Reprint lives only here. Kenneth: the common question is "which version am I printing", so a reprint must be attached to a specific G-code, never to a project or a printer.

### The screen

- Full view in place of the plater, like Home. Top bar: back arrow, "Print history", preferences gear. No printer chip, no plate button.
- Home and Project are the roots; Print history is always a leaf. Back returns to where it was opened from. Nothing opens on top of it: Open in chat and the printer link go to a root.
- Filters are removable chips ("Project: Garage bracket ×", "Printer: Bambu X1C ×"). Where you came from sets the first chip; remove it and the list widens to everything. Entries are grouped by day, newest first. A search box filters by text.

### Ways in

- Home header: a "Print history" link, unfiltered.
- Each Home project card: a history line ("2 prints · 1 printing now", "1 print · finished Sun") that opens the screen filtered to the project. No failure badge.
- Each Home printer card: a history line ("12 prints · 1 printing now") filtered to the printer.
- Project pane, Project tab: the Print history view is now one row (count, latest outcome) with a chevron into the screen. A project that never printed says "Nothing printed or exported yet".

### The chat

- When a G-code leaves the project, one marker line between turns: "▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history". Nothing else.
- Nothing about a print going wrong is recorded or drawn anywhere. The person tells the agent in chat ("it shifted off the plate"); the agent reads the recent G-codes and their settings from the history in its state and reasons from there. There is no Discuss link, no attachment and no recording tool.

### What is deliberately not drawn

- No Stale badge, no live progress card, no completed-print card in the chat, no entry with zero destinations, no failure state of any kind. Slicing writes nothing.

## Decision history

| When | What happened |
|---|---|
| Aug 7 – Sep 1 | Old Design project: setup card, "Prints" chip, "the chat is the timeline". Phase 6 (51a97b1bdf, 2026-09-01) adds BuildRecord, ExportedCopyRecord, PhysicalPrintRecord with chat cards. |
| Sep 10 | Kenneth: slicing writes nothing; entries only for G-code that left the project; no Stale. |
| Sep 11 | "Revert here" removed (dcb06059f3). |
| Oct 2–3 | Print history moves to the Project tab in the left pane (`Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp`). |
| Oct 26 | dbec3e3a38 removes BuildRecord and ExportedCopyRecord, adds `SentRecord`. 71c1791e39 (docs only) specifies that sending goes through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog and that an agent tool `print_dialog_open` may open it; the tool was never implemented. |
| Oct 27 morning | Canvas named the source of truth; chat-entry boards redrawn (G-code entry with rows, failed-print band). |
| Oct 27 evening | Redesign with Kenneth. Reasons, in his words: reprint belongs to the specific G-code, not the project; a failure in an old chat is strange when the person is in a new one; the history page is the natural home for the story and for file verification; printer and project histories are one table with two filters; a full view, since a column makes the navigation strange. Boards drawn and old ones retired the same day. |
| Oct 27 later | In a forked session Kenneth settled the record: file-bytes hash as the id, one record with destination and print lists replacing the separate events, G-code copies kept in the aux dir with a cap. Relayed to this doc by that session. |
| Oct 27 later still | In another forked session Kenneth removed every failure state ("I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed"): no Failed / Didn't go well rows, no badge, no Discuss, history-06 deleted. Relayed by that session; this session dropped Cancelled with them. |

## What the code does today (branch `jusprin-newui`, checked 2026-10-27 at 74951a60fd)

Paths below are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Line numbers are from this checkout and will drift.

### The ledger that exists but is never written

- `Agent/ManufacturingHistory.hpp`: `SentRecord` (sent_at, delivery_confirmed_at, conversation_id, plate, printer, material, `manufacturing_input_hash`, statistics) and `PhysicalPrintRecord` (outcome completed | failed | cancelled, failure, sent_id, conversation_id, after_message_id, `output_hash`, `gcode_hash`, stopped_percent, statistics). `ManufacturingHistory.cpp:14` has `sha256_hex()` and `:25` `manufacturing_input_hash()`, which hash the plate's presets and transforms, not an output file. `output_hash` and `gcode_hash` are serialized (`ProjectStateDocument.cpp:269`, `:1039`) but nothing computes them.
- `Agent/ProjectStateDocument.hpp:264-275`: `add_sent`, `confirm_delivery`, `add_physical_print`, `sent()`, `physical_prints()`. A print must point at an existing Sent event. `Agent/ProjectPersistence.hpp:87-92`: `subscribe_ledger` / `notify_ledger_changed`, used by the left pane (`Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp:124`).
- **No production code calls any of the writers.** Only `tests/agent/test_project_state.cpp` and `tests/shell/figma_timeline_fixture.cpp:113` do.

### Readers of the ledger, all to be redrawn

- `Home/ProjectStatus.cpp:5` `ledger_status`: Draft / Sent / Completed from the latest Sent event and latest completed print. Failed and cancelled are ignored. "Printing" comes from the live printer, not the ledger (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:242-267` matches a printer's `subtask_name` to the project name).
- `Shell/ProjectPaneModel.cpp` `build_print_history` and `Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp`: the old Print history list in the Project tab.
- `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:782` `send_state` sends `physicalPrints` (`:872`, built by `physical_print_json` at `:192`); Sent events are not sent to the page. `AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx:112` renders `ManufacturingHistoryCard` from them (`:206`); its "Discuss this failure" is a plain `sendMessage` in `AgentUI/src/App.tsx:498`. Types: `PhysicalPrintInfo` (`AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts:721`) and `StatePayload.physicalPrints` (`:1002`). All of this goes away; the chat keeps only the marker line.

### Export: where a file leaves

- OrcaSlicer's export: `src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:15051` `Plater::export_gcode` fixes the output path, `Plater::priv::export_gcode` (`:8226`, `:8259`) schedules `BackgroundSlicingProcess::export_gcode` (`src/slic3r/GUI/BackgroundSlicingProcess.cpp:857`), which copies the temp G-code to the final path and queues `EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED` with that path (`:899`). **Trap:** it runs `gcode_add_line_number` after posting the event, so the bytes can still change after the event; hash after the process reports completion (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `Plater.cpp:9911`, which already shows the "export finished" notification from `last_output_path` at `:10043`). `Plater::priv::on_export_finished` (`:9825`) is bound at `:5298` and its body is `#if 0`.
- Sliced 3MF export: `Plater::export_gcode_3mf` (`:15157`) writes synchronously through `export_3mf` (`:15221`).
- JusPrin's `export_file` tool: defined in `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1256` (handler `ToolHandler::ExportFile`, in-app and MCP), dispatched in `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1726`, written by `Workspace/OrcaOutputs.cpp:346` `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::export_file` (a `copy_file` of the plate's slice result for G-code; `Plater::export_3mf` for 3MF). Its `ExportResult` (`Workspace/Workspace.hpp:1072`) has paths and sizes, no hash. The tool's result JSON carries `files`, `bytes`, `sliceWarnings`, no hash.

### Send: where a file goes to a printer

- The Print action in the status row (`Shell/StatusRow.cpp:584`) fires `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_PRINT_PLATE`, handled by `Plater::priv::on_action_print_plate` (`Plater.cpp:10251`).
- Bambu, Select Machine dialog (Send always starts the print): `src/slic3r/GUI/SelectMachine.cpp:2381` `on_send_print` builds a `PrintJob` (`:2471`), runs it (`:2588`); on success `PrintJob::process` queues `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/PrintJob.cpp:668`), handled by `Plater::print_job_finished` (`Plater.cpp:16575`).
- Bambu, Send to Printer dialog (upload to SD only, never prints): `src/slic3r/GUI/SendToPrinter.cpp:809` `on_ok` creates a `SendJob` (`:951`); `SendJob` queues `EVT_SEND_FINISHED` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/SendJob.cpp:364`), handled by `Plater::send_job_finished` (`Plater.cpp:16602`).
- Print hosts (Moonraker, OctoPrint): `Plater::send_gcode_legacy` (`Plater.cpp:16304`) reads the dialog's `post_action` (`:16473`; `StartPrint` = print after upload), stored in `PrintHostJob.upload_data.post_action` (`src/slic3r/Utils/PrintHost.hpp:39`). The upload completes in `PrintHostJobQueue::priv::perform_job` (`src/slic3r/Utils/PrintHost.cpp:357`, `emit_progress(100)` at `:368`), which reaches `PrintHostQueueDialog::on_progress` (`src/slic3r/GUI/PrintHostDialogs.cpp:1382`). There is no other success callback.
- **The fork binds none of `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, `EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED` or the print-host events.**
- **Correction to earlier notes:** commit 71c1791e39 ("Send a print through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog") changed three docs only. The `print_dialog_open` tool exists as a specification in `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:571` (seams named there: `Plater::priv::on_action_print_plate`, `Plater::send_gcode_legacy`) and nowhere in code.

### Printer status: where outcomes would come from

- Bambu fields in `src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceManager.hpp`: `print_status` (`:478`; FINISH, RUNNING, PAUSE, FAILED…), `mc_print_stage` (`:393`), `mc_print_percent` (`:397`), `print_error` (`:404`), `job_id_` / `task_id_` (`:643`), `subtask_name` (`:673`). Parsed in `MachineObject::parse_json` (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceManager.cpp:2569`; percent `:3069`, error `:3096`, state via `set_print_state` `:3185`, subtask name `:3196`). Messages arrive through `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:2157` (cloud) and `:2203` (LAN).
- The fork only polls these: `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:48` `machine_is_printing`, polled by `Home/HomeWebView.cpp:119` `on_live_tick` while Home is visible; also `PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp:78`, `Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:278`, `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:781`. **No fork class observes status changes.** A writer of printing / finished (FAILED and a person's stop are ignored on purpose) must hook `DeviceManager` / `GUI_App` message handling or poll `get_my_machine_list()` on its own timer, and must run whether or not Home or the project is visible.
- Matching a printer's job to a G-code record: today Home matches `subtask_name` to the project name. The new record should store what the send gave the printer (the uploaded file name, Bambu's job or task id when the job reports one) so a status change maps to one record, not to a project.
- Moonraker / Klipper: `Printers/HostLaneReader.cpp:53` `LaneReader` (a subclass of Orca's `Moonraker`) polls filament lanes only; `HostStatus` (`Printers/HostLanes.hpp:70`) has no print progress, and Orca's `src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp` never queries `print_stats`. Print-host outcomes need a new reader; the fake Moonraker simulator lives on branch `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under `tests/printer_sim/`.
- Test double: `Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp:169-232` simulates `mc_percent`, `gcode_state` (RUNNING, PAUSE, FINISH, FAILED) and `print_error`; a test should assert that FAILED writes nothing; `Testing/README.md` is the operator guide (enable with `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf`, keep a Bambu preset selected; a control file drives the state).

### Home: where the screen goes

- `Home/HomeWebView.hpp:30` (`wxPanel` around a `wxWebView`) hosts the Home page and owns `Home/HomeHost.hpp:22`; Orca-facing work is behind `Home/HomeBackend.hpp:29` (`IHomeBackend`), implemented by `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`.
- `Shell/ShellController.cpp:601` creates the view beside the Notebook; `on_page_changed` (`:1561`) shows Home and hides the Notebook and status row when the selection is `MainFrame::tpHome` (`:1570-1583`); `Shell/StatusRow.cpp:385` `request_home` is how the person gets there. The project stays loaded underneath, so Back from Print history to the project is instant.
- `HomeUI/src/App.tsx` is one screen with no routing (Projects at about `:180`, first run `:215`, Printers `:252`); state in `HomeUI/src/state/store.ts:16` (`HomeState`: projects, printers); page and host messages in `HomeUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts:17-43`, shared schema in `resources/jusprin/home/protocol.json`. The Print history screen is a second screen in this page, with a `screen` field in the state and host messages to open it with a filter and to go back. Opening it from the project means: select `tpHome` and tell the page which screen and filter to show.
- Project list: `OrcaHomeBackend::recent_projects` (`:229`) calls `ProjectAutosave::projects()` (`Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:778`), which scans every folder under `<data_dir>/jusprin/projects/` that has a `HEAD` file and attaches a `Ledger{sent, prints}` from each project's document (`:803`).

### Persistence, and the cross-project list

- Managed mode (the app's normal mode): the project root is `<data_dir>/jusprin/projects/<projectId>/` (`Shell/ShellController.cpp:301`; on this Mac `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/projects`). The state document is `current-state.json` (`{schema: 2, state}`), written by `ProjectVersionStore::publish_document` (`Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:814`) and read at `:621`; `ProjectStateDocument::load` / `dump` (`Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp:440`, `:459`). Checkpoints live beside it: `HEAD`, `versions/<id>/manifest.json` + `metadata.3mf`, `resources/<id>.zip` (`ProjectVersionStore.cpp:584-614`).
- **Kept G-code copies go here**: `<project root>/gcode/<hash>.gcode` (name to confirm in code review), capped at N per project, pruned when a new one is written. This is the "aux directory next to the checkpoints" in the decision. Exported 3MFs do not carry it.
- Legacy mode (no managed root): `<aux>/JusPrin/state.json` via `write_state_to` (`Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:451`), packed into the 3MF (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2693`). The history record must round-trip there too, without the kept copies.
- **There is no cross-project index**, and none is needed for the first version: the unfiltered and printer-filtered views can be built the way Home already builds its list, by scanning every project folder and reading its records (`ProjectAutosave::projects()`). Add an index file only if that scan proves slow with many projects; the Home live tick already does it on every refresh. A record must carry the project id and name so a row can say which project it belongs to and open it.
- Other per-user files for reference: `jusprin/mcp.json` (`ShellController.cpp:301-340`), `printer_facts.json` (`Shell/AgentPane.cpp:37`), `jusprin/v1-import.json`, and app-config sections `jusprin_agent`, `jusprin_server`, `jusprin_verified_connections`.
- **Migration**: schema 2 documents may contain `sent` and `physicalPrints` arrays written by tests or by the Phase 6 era. `load` must accept them without error and drop them (or fold them into records by `manufacturing_input_hash` if cheap). No shipped build ever wrote them, so there is no user data to preserve. `.3mf` backward compatibility still applies to the legacy `state.json`.

### Chat attachment and model context

- (For reference only, no longer used by this design: the print-issue attachment path is `issueContext` on `MessageInfo`, `AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts:142-145`, built by `Shell/ShellController.cpp:1095` `submit_issue` and `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:2651` `submit_issue_message`, reaching the model as a `<print_issue>` block.)
- **`AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts` is the fixed system prompt**, four static sections pinned by `projectInstructions.test.ts`. Situational text belongs in state, not there (Kenneth's rule: standing prompt = principles). The state the model reads is built by `AgentHost::make_agent_request` (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:2748`) into `AgentRequest` (`Agent/AgentService.hpp:97`) and emitted by `workspace_json` (`Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:36`, `:203`, as `<workspace>`). A manufacturing-history section is a new field on `AgentRequest`, filled in `make_agent_request`, emitted from `workspace_json`, plus at most one Grounding line in the prompt.
- Tools: definitions in `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:747` `make_definitions()` (`export_file` at `:1256`), handler enum `Agent/ToolRegistry.hpp:48`, dispatch `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`, tests `tests/agent/test_tool_registry.cpp`. Error codes in `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp` (one list, same in-app and MCP). New tools: `print_dialog_open` (specified, not built) and a reprint variant of it that opens the send dialog with a kept copy. No tool records print outcomes: outcomes come only from the printer.

## Rules that apply to this work

- **Fork stewardship** (`agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`): export, send and printer status live in OrcaSlicer-owned files. Bind the existing events (`EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED`, `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, the print-host progress) from fork code rather than editing the handlers; one seam each. The PR must carry the rebase simulation (`git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD`) with both endpoint commits, an account of every upstream line changed, and a statement of what the fork now owns.
- **UI values** (`agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, "Writing UI code"): every colour, radius, font and control size comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, through `ShellTheme` and `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp` natively and through the CSS variables on the web pages. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first.
- **Wording**: a file is exported, sent, opened or loaded, never "arrived" (`AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the model-facing text).
- **Errors**: no catch-and-log; invalid transitions (a print without its G-code, a hash mismatch on a kept copy) fail visibly.
- **Working docs** stay untracked; commit code, tests and standing guides only.

## How to test

- **Catch2, no GUI**: `tests/agent/test_project_state.cpp` holds the ledger cases (`:215`, `:485-641`) and the ledger-subscriber cases (`:1242-1284`); rewrite them for the G-code record (create-or-append on export and send, outcome rows, the migration of schema-2 `sent` / `physicalPrints`, the kept-copy cap). Target: `agent_bridge_tests` (`tests/agent/CMakeLists.txt:3`); run with `ctest --test-dir build/arm64/tests/agent --output-on-failure`. Home and pane models: `tests/jusprin/test_project_status.cpp`, `test_project_pane_model.cpp`, `test_home_host.cpp`, `test_home_snapshot.cpp`, `test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`.
- **Vitest**: `cd src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI && npm test` and the same under `HomeUI` (setup in `src/test/setup.ts`). The marker line gets a component test in AgentUI; the Print history screen, its filters and the one-level back get tests in HomeUI. Prove a guard test fails first by injecting the violation.
- **Shell harness** (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`, target `shell_integration_harness`, modes documented in its header comment, `main` at `:11914`): `--figma-timeline-capture <dir>` seeds history through `tests/shell/figma_timeline_fixture.cpp:113` and screenshots the Agent pane; its print-history checks at `:1724-1729` assert the old cards and must be rewritten for the marker. Add a `--print-history` mode that exports and sends with the fake printer, drives a FINISH state through the control file (and a FAILED state, asserting it writes nothing), then opens the screen from Home and from the project pane and captures it. Always run with an isolated `--datadir`; never drive another JusPrin instance.
- **End to end on the Mac**: build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all -- -j4` after checking `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`; run the built app with the fake Bambu printer (`Testing/README.md`), slice, Print, confirm the record appears in `current-state.json` and the kept copy under the project root, then finish the print through the control file and check the Home card line and the history row. Export a G-code to the desktop, edit the file, and check the "changed" state. The bundle id is `io.jusprin.JusPrin`.
- **Live printer**: only after the fake passes; the delivery and "started" facts for Bambu come from `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, which the fake also raises.

## What the app needs (in rough order)

1. **A G-code record**: file-bytes hash (the id), name, plate, time, stats, printer, material, profile, `manufacturing_input_hash` (the checkpoint link), the chat and message it went out from, and its lists of destinations and prints. It replaces `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` in `ManufacturingHistory.hpp` and the `add_sent` / `add_physical_print` API in `ProjectStateDocument`. Nothing in the app ever wrote those, so there is nothing to preserve beyond a migration note: a 3MF that carries them (possible only from tests or the Phase 6 era) is read without error and the old events are dropped or, if cheap, folded into records keyed by their `manufacturing_input_hash`.
2. **Writers**: the export path (`EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED` after `on_process_completed`, and the `export_file` tool) and the send paths (`EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, print-host progress 100 with `post_action`) hash the file bytes before the file leaves, then create or append the record; printer status writes printing and finished only.
2a. **Kept copies**: on every send or export, copy the G-code into the project's aux directory beside the checkpoints; keep the last N per project and mark older records "file no longer kept, re-slice".
3. **File checks**: hash the exported file when the screen opens and on demand; three states (matches, changed, not found).
4. **The screen** as a second screen of the Home web page (`HomeUI`, which has no routing today), with the filter chips and the one-level back; host messages to open it with a filter and to go back; the ways in: Home header link, card lines, project pane row. Opening from the project selects `tpHome` and names the screen and filter.
5. **Print again** for a recorded G-code: open OrcaSlicer's send dialog for the kept copy (step 2a) instead of the current slice. The `print_dialog_open` tool is specified in the tool guide but not built; build it so both the screen and the agent use it. When the copy is gone, the entry offers re-slice instead.
6. **Chat**: the marker line replaces `ManufacturingHistoryCard`; Open in chat scrolls to it.
7. **Model context**: a manufacturing-history field on `AgentRequest`, filled in `make_agent_request` and emitted by `workspace_json`, so the agent knows what left the project, how each print ended, and can diff a failed G-code's settings (by `manufacturing_input_hash`) against the current setup. Not a new prompt section.

## Open questions for Kenneth

The record's id, shape and kept bytes, and the removal of every failure state, were decided on 2026-10-27 (see "The record" above). Still open:

1. **When files are re-checked**: on screen open only, or also when the project opens (to set the Home card's "file not found" status)?
2. **N**, the number of kept G-code copies per project, is chosen in code; say it in the PR.

## Working on the canvas

- Run `Artifact` read on the canvas url (plain, no path) once per session before publishing, or the publish is refused as "not viewed the latest version". Then read each file you will change with `path`.
- Publish with `url`, `root` set to a folder holding `project/…`, `file_path` the absolute path of one changed file, and the other changed files in `files`. Send `project/canvas.json` only when a board's size, position, page or title changes. Someone else may publish between your read and your publish (the version id changed twice during this work); re-read `canvas.json` right before an index publish.
- After every publish, stop the comment watch (`ArtifactComments` watch, `on: false`), or this session auto-answers comments meant for another session.
- Local render: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/tools/composer/render.py <dir with ds/ and canvas.json> <out dir> <board>`, absolute paths. It needs `ds/jusprin/tokens.css` and `components/bundle.css` in that dir (read them from the canvas). `<dc-import>` components render blank: header, setup card, printer chip, composer, plates pane.
- The history boards were generated by two scripts in this session's scratchpad (`history-design/build_history_boards.py` draws the six boards and patches main-05 from one `entry()` template; `retire_old_boards.py` patches main-07, main-09, plates-26e3 and comp-plates-pane). Scratchpads are wiped on restart; the published boards are the source now. Copy markup from them and from `ds/jusprin/components/bundle.css`, never from the frozen canvas.

1	# Handoff: G-code and print history
2	
3	Written 2026-10-27, rewritten the same evening after Kenneth and I redesigned it. Temporary working doc: keep it untracked, never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
4	
5	## In short
6	
7	JusPrin keeps **one record per G-code** that left a project: where it went (exported files, sends to printers) and what the printer reported about each print of it (printing, finished). Slicing by itself writes nothing. **No failure state anywhere** (decided 2026-10-27): there is no reliable way to know a print failed, so nothing records, badges or discusses a failure.
8	
9	That record is shown on **one full-view screen, "Print history"**, reached from Home and from the project. The chat only gets a one-line marker when a G-code leaves the project. The old design, where the chat held G-code entries and a dark failed-print band, is retired: its boards are deleted or redrawn. A print that went wrong is something the person tells the agent in chat; the history gives the G-code and its settings for that conversation.
10	
11	The app is far behind: it persists `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` but never writes them outside tests, has no export record, and the model never sees print history. The next job is to implement the drawn design.
12	
13	## Where the design lives
14	
15	- **Current canvas, the source of truth:** https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ ("JusPrin v2"), version 1793148719-e71c or later (checked against the published file list on 2026-10-27: history-01…05 present, history-06 and agent-ui-01 gone, comp-plates-pane, main-05/07/09 and plates-26e3 updated). New page **"Print history"** (id `print-history`):
16	  - `history-01-all-prints`: the screen with no filter.
17	  - `history-02-project-garage-bracket`: filtered to one project.
18	  - `history-03-printer-bambu-x1c`: filtered to one printer.
19	  - `history-04-entry-states`: every row state of an entry, and the no-failure-state rule. This replaces the deleted `agent-ui-01` chat-timeline state matrix.
20	  - `history-05-ways-in`: the Home header link, project cards, printer cards and the project pane row that open the screen.
21	  - (`history-06-discuss-in-current-chat` was drawn and deleted the same day when failure states were dropped.)
22	  - Main Page: `main-05`, `main-07`, `main-09` now show one-line G-code markers in the chat instead of entries and a band.
23	  - Plates & Project Pane: `plates-26e3` ("Project · print history row") and `plates-26e4` ("Project · never printed"; the file is still named `count-only-print-history`). Both import `comp-plates-pane`, whose Project tab was redrawn.
24	- **Frozen, history only:** the previous canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, the old Claude Design project "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts", and Figma (retired 2026-10-20). They show the chat-entry design and how it was reached, never the current design.
25	- Memory note for agents: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/print-history-screen-design.md`.
26	
27	## The design (decided 2026-10-27)
28	
29	### The record
30	
31	Every print has three keys: the project it came from, the G-code it ran, and the printer it ran on. That is one table. The project view and the printer view are filters over it, so they can never disagree.
32	
33	The **G-code record** (decided 2026-10-27 in a forked session, relayed here by that session; Kenneth's words were "go with your recommendations"):
34	
35	- **Identity:** a hash of the G-code file bytes, computed at export or send time, before the file leaves. The existing `manufacturing_input_hash` stays beside it as the link to the checkpoint. Displayed as eight hex digits in two groups ("a71f 8c04").
36	- **Shape:** one record per G-code holding its lists of destinations (exports, sends) and prints. Export and send create the record or append to it. The separate `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` events are replaced, not kept beside it.
37	- **Bytes:** JusPrin keeps a copy of every sent or exported G-code in the project's aux directory next to the checkpoints, capped at the last N G-codes per project (N chosen in code). Older entries show a "file no longer kept, re-slice" state instead of Print again.
38	
39	An **entry** is one G-code:
40	
41	- Header: name (the exported file name, else the plate name), short hash in monospace as a secondary id, the stats line ("2h 34m · 69 g · 181 layers"), the time. The project name shows only when no project filter is on.
42	- "Made with Bambu X1C · Gray PETG · 0.20 Strong · Open in chat". Open in chat jumps to the marker in the chat where this G-code went out.
43	- One row per **destination**:
44	  - Export: `matches, checked just now` (green check); `changed outside JusPrin` (greyed, warning glyph, Export again); `not found` (greyed, Export again). Greyed means opacity, never strike-through. Export again writes a new file beside a changed one, it does not overwrite.
45	  - Send: `sending…`; `sent, delivery not confirmed`; `on the printer's SD · started` or `· not started`. A send never gets a check mark: only a hashed file is verified. Use the printer's own name, not its model.
46	- One row per **print**, only what the printer reports: Printing (the only live fact drawn; progress stays on the printer card) and Finished. **No Failed, Didn't go well or Cancelled row.** Kenneth, 2026-10-27: "I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed." Cancelled goes with them because a Bambu reports a person's stop as a failed state and the two cannot be told apart. A print that stopped early simply never gets a Finished row.
47	- Actions: **Print again** and **Export…**. Reprint lives only here. Kenneth: the common question is "which version am I printing", so a reprint must be attached to a specific G-code, never to a project or a printer.
48	
49	### The screen
50	
51	- Full view in place of the plater, like Home. Top bar: back arrow, "Print history", preferences gear. No printer chip, no plate button.
52	- Home and Project are the roots; Print history is always a leaf. Back returns to where it was opened from. Nothing opens on top of it: Open in chat and the printer link go to a root.
53	- Filters are removable chips ("Project: Garage bracket ×", "Printer: Bambu X1C ×"). Where you came from sets the first chip; remove it and the list widens to everything. Entries are grouped by day, newest first. A search box filters by text.
54	
55	### Ways in
56	
57	- Home header: a "Print history" link, unfiltered.
58	- Each Home project card: a history line ("2 prints · 1 printing now", "1 print · finished Sun") that opens the screen filtered to the project. No failure badge.
59	- Each Home printer card: a history line ("12 prints · 1 printing now") filtered to the printer.
60	- Project pane, Project tab: the Print history view is now one row (count, latest outcome) with a chevron into the screen. A project that never printed says "Nothing printed or exported yet".
61	
62	### The chat
63	
64	- When a G-code leaves the project, one marker line between turns: "▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history". Nothing else.
65	- Nothing about a print going wrong is recorded or drawn anywhere. The person tells the agent in chat ("it shifted off the plate"); the agent reads the recent G-codes and their settings from the history in its state and reasons from there. There is no Discuss link, no attachment and no recording tool.
66	
67	### What is deliberately not drawn
68	
69	- No Stale badge, no live progress card, no completed-print card in the chat, no entry with zero destinations, no failure state of any kind. Slicing writes nothing.
70	
71	## Decision history
72	
73	| When | What happened |
74	|---|---|
75	| Aug 7 – Sep 1 | Old Design project: setup card, "Prints" chip, "the chat is the timeline". Phase 6 (51a97b1bdf, 2026-09-01) adds BuildRecord, ExportedCopyRecord, PhysicalPrintRecord with chat cards. |
76	| Sep 10 | Kenneth: slicing writes nothing; entries only for G-code that left the project; no Stale. |
77	| Sep 11 | "Revert here" removed (dcb06059f3). |
78	| Oct 2–3 | Print history moves to the Project tab in the left pane (`Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp`). |
79	| Oct 26 | dbec3e3a38 removes BuildRecord and ExportedCopyRecord, adds `SentRecord`. 71c1791e39 (docs only) specifies that sending goes through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog and that an agent tool `print_dialog_open` may open it; the tool was never implemented. |
80	| Oct 27 morning | Canvas named the source of truth; chat-entry boards redrawn (G-code entry with rows, failed-print band). |
81	| Oct 27 evening | Redesign with Kenneth. Reasons, in his words: reprint belongs to the specific G-code, not the project; a failure in an old chat is strange when the person is in a new one; the history page is the natural home for the story and for file verification; printer and project histories are one table with two filters; a full view, since a column makes the navigation strange. Boards drawn and old ones retired the same day. |
82	| Oct 27 later | In a forked session Kenneth settled the record: file-bytes hash as the id, one record with destination and print lists replacing the separate events, G-code copies kept in the aux dir with a cap. Relayed to this doc by that session. |
83	| Oct 27 later still | In another forked session Kenneth removed every failure state ("I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed"): no Failed / Didn't go well rows, no badge, no Discuss, history-06 deleted. Relayed by that session; this session dropped Cancelled with them. |
84	
85	## What the code does today (branch `jusprin-newui`, checked 2026-10-27 at 74951a60fd)
86	
87	Paths below are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Line numbers are from this checkout and will drift.
88

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)

                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

## Known Issues and Workarounds

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp
// MinGW/CygWin slow linking workaround
// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

// Visual Studio 2017 raw string literal bug

// This disables expression stringification but works around the compiler bug

// Visual Studio 2022 spaceship operator issue

// Workaround: use clang-cl or avoid spaceship in assertions

### Catch2 v3 Features Available

The records are shown on one screen, Print history, the second screen of the Home page (`HomeUI/src/components/PrintHistory.tsx`). It is a leaf of Home and of the project: the gallery's header link, a project card's or printer card's history line, the project pane's Print history row and a chat marker's "history" link all open it, and where it was opened from sets its first filter. Back from the gallery stays in the page; opened from the project, the shell selects Home with the screen named (`ShellController::open_print_history`, sent as the `screen` message when Home comes on screen) and Back selects the tab it came from. The page asks for the entries (`history_request`) each time it opens and each time the host's state moves under it; `Home/PrintHistory` builds them from every project's records, pure and tested in `agent_bridge_tests`, with what only the application knows (preset labels, which printer card a printer is, the exported files' checks) passed in by `OrcaHomeBackend`. An exported file is hashed again when the screen asks, unless its size and time are as they were at the last hash. Export… writes the project's kept copy and records it; Export again on a changed file writes a new file beside it. Open in chat opens the project if another is open and asks the Agent page to show the chat and scroll to the marker (`reveal_item`). The page phrases every line; nothing records, badges or draws a failure.

Decided 2026-10-24. A file reaches JusPrin in a handful of ways, and they mean one of two things: **start from this file**, or **add this to the project I am working on**. The first is what a person means almost every time they bring a file in; the second is the minority case (a multi-part print), and the person signals it by aiming at the plate or by asking the agent. Because autosave keeps every project, starting a new project by mistake costs one click on Recent, while adding to the wrong project leaves a stray part in it. So every way in starts a new project unless the person aimed at the plate.

input.content:
Show every G-code that left a project on one Print history screen

The G-code records stage 1 writes are now shown on one screen, Print
history, the second screen of the Home page (boards history-01...05). One
entry per G-code, grouped by day, newest first: its name, short hash and
estimates, what it was made with, a row per destination (an export says
whether the file still holds what was written: matches, changed outside
JusPrin, not found; a send says whether delivery was confirmed and whether
it started the print) and a row per print as the printer reported it
(Printing with its progress, Finished). Nothing draws a failure: a print
that stopped early shows only when it started.

The project and the printer are filters over the one list, removable chips;
a search box narrows it further. Ways in: a Print history link in the
gallery header (unfiltered), a history line on each project card and each
printer card, one row on the project pane's Project tab (which replaces the
pane's own Print history view), and a "history" link on each chat marker.
Back returns to where the screen was opened from: the gallery stays in the
page; from the project the shell selects Home with the screen named and
Back selects the tab it came from. Open in chat opens the project if
another is open and scrolls its chat to the marker (reveal_item). Export…
writes the project's kept copy and records it; Export again on a changed
file writes a new file beside it, never over it.

Home/PrintHistory builds the entries and the card counts from every
project's records, pure and tested; OrcaHomeBackend passes in what only the
application knows (preset labels, which card a printer is, file checks,
